whatItFakes: A regional office of a firm (enterprise:corporate-office) sells its work as professional services to outside buyers, with demand sized from its own payroll like any firm's, in place of being paid by its parent firm's allocation.
why: No record names the parent firm of a town's regional office (town-workplaces.ts builds it as a plain town workplace), so there is no payer to allocate from. Left as the old branch-or-institution route it opened with $0 and its staff were never paid (Boulevard CA 0607694, seed pp-a: organization_cd524c66abde5ef1, work-relationship_9f0d2babaf670fc8 earned 347,556, paid 0). With the professional kind it ends the year with cash 9,508,565 and that job is paid.
replacement: A named parent-firm allocation: the office is paid by the firm it belongs to, read from firm ownership records, once those exist (world-corporate-office-opens-unfunded).

whatItFakes: Someone the director does not watch is talked about only for what their own events in the core's log record (a move, an illness, a birth). A new job of theirs is never news, because a hire writes no event naming the person: the director infers a job start only for people it watches, by comparing their job before and after (src/director/ledger.ts, 'job-started').
why: Found while building words-talk-never-adds-the-person-to-who-you-know (Nov 11, 2026): the jobs engine's hire changes the person's job record and writes no event to logByPerson, so recordedMoments has nothing to read for an unwatched person's new job.
replacement: The jobs engine's hire writes one event naming the person and the employer (the event it already describes), which recordedMoments reads like a move.
